title: Online Banking Licences for Internet Companies that Provide Mobile Payment Solutions
what_it_is: Online Banking Licences for Internet Companies that Provide Mobile Payment Solutions

sections.label: Internet-only bank licensing framework
sections.summary: MAS' bank licensing framework can accommodate Internet-only banks, which operate within the same licensing and regulatory regime as conventional banks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS' existing bank licensing framework can accommodate Internet-only banks to operate in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As the risks posed by Internet-only banks are not fundamentally different from those posed by conventional banks, they will operate within the same licensing and regulatory regime as conventional banks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: But most Internet companies will not require a banking licence unless they intend to take deposits and grant loans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: If they are offering mainly payment solutions, depending on the specific type of payment service they provide, they may be subject to a narrow set of regulatory requirements pertinent to that payment service.

sections.label: Activity-based payments regulatory framework
sections.summary: MAS has put out for consultation a new, streamlined activity-based regulatory framework for payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To better calibrate its regulatory requirements to the various modes of innovative payment services, MAS has put out for consultation a new, streamlined activity-based regulatory framework for payments.

sections.label: Central Addressing Scheme for FAST
sections.summary: By the end of this year, the industry will incorporate a Central Addressing Scheme into FAST, using a proxy such as NRIC or mobile number.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What is not so convenient is that it is based on bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, by the end of this year, the industry will be incorporating within FAST a Central Addressing Scheme (CAS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What CAS allows FAST to do is to have a proxy for our bank accounts, using, say, our NRIC number or mobile phone number.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Which means once this is in place, there is potential for us to make payments, not different from WeChat or Alipay.
